source: VegasInsider 4-book devigged win totals (2026-08-09) normalized to 272; per-game probabilities refit to those totals over the nflverse 2026 schedule
note: A private eight-person pool: four NFL teams each, all 32 owned, total regular-season wins the only criterion. Expected wins are devigged from four books and normalized to 272; they are NOT the posted lines, and `line` carries those separately. Nothing here is graded — the 2026 season has not started, every wins_tracker row reads zero, and no figure on this surface is a result. `drafters`, `undrafted`, `board` and `diagnostics` are derived from `picks` by scripts/team_draft_pool.py and are rewritten on every run.

field_notes.line: Median posted regular-season win total. Half-point lines are the book's.
field_notes.ew: Devigged expected wins, normalized so all 32 sum to 272. Not the posted line.
field_notes.sd: Season win standard deviation from the upstream simulation.
field_notes.dist: Probability mass by final win count, 0 through 17. Sums to 1 within rounding.
field_notes.schedule: 17 games: week, opponent, home flag, and this team's win probability.
field_notes.schedule[].wp: The payload's original per-game probability. Coherent game by game; does not re-add to `ew`.
field_notes.schedule[].wpf: The same game after the schedule was refit onto `ew`. This is what the simulation uses.
field_notes.simulation: Monte Carlo over `live`, game by game, on top of whatever is banked. Finishing probabilities, not a forecast; nothing graded.
field_notes.schedule[].live: What this game is worth right now: a settled result, a market price, a model price, or the frozen preseason number. `tier` says which.
field_notes.schedule[].tier: settled | market | model | preseason. Every game carries its own provenance.
field_notes.teams[].banked: Wins actually recorded. A tie counts half.
field_notes.teams[].remaining: Sum of the live probabilities for games not yet played.
field_notes.teams[].projected: banked + remaining. The in-season number. `ew` stays frozen at the draft-day devig beside it.
field_notes.overlap: Sparse symmetric head-to-head game counts. 2 = division rival, 1 = other, absent = 0.
field_notes.wins_tracker: Actual wins, by round, per drafter. Every value is zero — no game has been played.
field_notes.board[].delta: Chosen team's expected wins minus the best still available. Descriptive, not a grade.

tier_meaning: Pup — live and useful, not yet validated. It may compute real answers and still have open questions about calibration, assumptions, data quality or edge. Everything starts here.

tiebreakers: total playoff wins among the four teams
total regular-season point differential among the four teams

resolution: settled — the game was played; banked, not projected
market — unplayed with a real price; market primacy does not lapse in-season
preseason — the frozen 2026-08-09 devigged total, refit onto expected wins
basis.switch: data-driven: one settled game anywhere flips the payload to the composite. No date is hardcoded.

schedule_fit.method: per-team logit offsets solved by Newton so each team's 17 fitted game probabilities sum to its expected wins; complementarity and the 272-win league total hold by construction

simulation.method: game-level Bernoulli over the refitted schedule; one win per game, so every simulated season pays exactly 272
simulation.first_place_ties_broken: at random — the league's real tiebreakers (playoff wins, then point differential) are not in this payload

checks.label: Expected wins sum to 272
checks.detail: 272.01 against a league total of 272. The teams carry two decimals each, so a drift of a hundredth or two is the rounding and nothing else; anything larger means the devig was not renormalized.

checks.label: Head-to-head matrix is symmetric and complete
checks.detail: 0 asymmetric entries, 272 games total (expect 272), 0 teams not playing exactly 17.

checks.label: Every game's two win probabilities sum to 1
checks.detail: 0 games where the two sides do not complement. The schedule is one coherent set of games, not 32 independent lists.

checks.label: The supplied game probabilities re-add to expected wins
checks.detail: Summing a team's 17 supplied probabilities lands at most 0.0050 wins from its expected-wins figure (worst: ATL). That is four-decimal rounding across 17 games, not a disagreement — the ladder and the schedule strip are one number.

checks.label: Win distributions run above expected wins at the bottom of the board
checks.detail: The mean of the 0-17 distribution sits up to 0.36 wins from expected wins (MIA). The gap is positive for the worst teams and negative for the best, which is what truncation at 0 and 17 does to a distribution built around a mean near the edge. The curves are the shape of a season, not a second estimate of its total.

checks.label: Each win distribution sums to 1
checks.detail: Worst total mass is off by 0.00020 — four-decimal rounding across 18 buckets.

checks.label: The draft log is a valid snake
checks.detail: 32 of 32 picks recorded. 0 out of turn, 0 teams taken twice, 0 unknown abbreviations.

checks.label: Rostered wins plus the pool still add to the league total
checks.detail: 272.01 on rosters, 0.00 still on the board, 272.01 together. With every pick made, the eight roster totals must sum to 272 and one drafter's gain is another's loss — that is the whole game.

checks.label: The refitted schedule does re-add to expected wins
checks.detail: Solved in 60 Newton steps; the worst team is now 0.0003 wins from its expected-wins figure, against 0.00 before the refit. The residual cannot reach zero: the 32 expected-win values sum to 272.01 rather than 272, and a schedule of whole games always pays exactly 272, so that one hundredth has to live somewhere. `wp` is untouched — `wpf` sits beside it and the simulation uses only `wpf`.

checks.label: Simulated roster totals land on each roster's ew total
checks.detail: Across 100,000 simulated seasons the worst roster mean sits 0.029 wins from its ew total. That agreement is the refit and the banked floor working together — simulating the raw preseason schedule instead would have put a roster up to 2.7 wins away from the number printed on its own card, and re-simulating settled games would widen every range for the rest of the season.

checks.label: A tie for first is common, and this payload cannot break one
checks.detail: 14.7% of simulated seasons end with two or more rosters level at the top — roughly one in 7. The league breaks that on total playoff wins and then point differential; neither is in this payload, so the simulation breaks it at random and the page reports the rate instead of pretending to a winner. The simulation also has no tie OUTCOME: every game is decided, so no half-wins are produced.

checks.label: The simulation is running on complete rosters
checks.detail: Every roster has all four teams, so the finishing probabilities are about the league as drafted.

checks.label: Banked plus projected still totals the season
checks.detail: 0.00 banked + 272.01 projected = 272.01 against 272. 0 of 272 games are played. Per-game basis: preseason 544.

checks.label: The payload is in preseason mode
checks.detail: Nothing has been played, so every game carries the frozen 2026-08-09 devigged total refit onto expected wins. The moment one game is settled this flips to the composite by itself — no date is hardcoded.

checks.label: Two roster standard deviations, and they disagree
checks.detail: The upstream simulation and the quadrature-plus-head-to-head calculation sit within 0.84 wins of each other (worst: Jared). They diverge most for rosters with internal games, and the simulation is the smaller of the two — it also draws correlated team strength, which quadrature cannot see. The page shows the simulated figure wherever it exists and says when it is falling back.
